series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 4.2 · October 2026
title: The Climate Investment Trust

slides.title: The Climate Investment Trust: Hold Capital, Lend Its Strength
slides.subtitle: A buffer fund that insures policy guarantees, invests in clean energy and holds national climate accounts
slides.message: Donors will not vote for large cash rewards. A trust that holds capital behind policy guarantees delivers about 80 dollars of interest savings per donor dollar on the development banks' loss record, and 2.7 in a stress case without their preferred-creditor status.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.title: Cash rewards for national climate policy are too large to be voted

stats.label: a year to pay $100 per tonne for a 10% cut in fossil CO₂ (37.8 Gt in 2024)
pledged at launch (Nov 2025) to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, against a $25bn sponsor target
of reward per donor dollar from a fund that pays out, and then it is gone

slides.text: A guarantee saves the borrower the whole credit spread but costs the guarantor only its expected loss. Someone has to hold the capital behind it.
slides.source: Global Carbon Budget 2025 (Friedlingstein et al. 2026); WRI (Barber et al. 2025).

slides.title: A trust separates who pays, who decides and who benefits

points.text: a development bank manages the Trust under its trust fund rules.
each participating country has an account for its post-2050 population, drawn only after 2050.
A country pledges its balance to cut the rate on its green borrowing.
Taxing a sovereign is not; deducting from a balance it does not yet control is. Accounts build a constituency for persistence.

slides.source: Working paper 4.2, Section 3; Stretton, Time and Chance (manuscript), ch. 20.

slides.title: One pool does three jobs, and the buffer is kept apart from the investments
rows: The Trust's buffer, in high-grade bonds
AAA backer: MDB or rated sovereign
Regional fund holds the first-loss tranche of operating pools
Feebate between accounts: credits and debits cancel
slides.note: The buffer never holds clean power equity: it would lose value in the same crises that trigger guarantee calls.

slides.title: Each dollar held delivers the spread saved divided by the expected loss: about 80 on the banks' record

points.text: 0.77% calls a year, 95.1% recovered. A 0.5% buffer keeps exhaustion at 1% a year; $5bn supports ~$1tn on paper.
3% calls, 37% loss. A 9.25% buffer; $5bn supports $54bn; 2.7 per dollar.

slides.source: GEMs (EIB 2025); Cruces and Trebesch (2013); author's calculation, 20 programs, correlation 0.2, 3-point spread.

slides.title: Three conditions decide how much of the 80 the Trust delivers

points.text: Governments repay development banks first, but the practice is informal. Book the Trust's claims through a bank, or plan for the stress case.
Holding the stress-case buffer while losses follow the record cuts the reward to ~13 per dollar (2% carry) until the Trust has its own record.
A call costs a year's debt service now, recovered later. Paying it from the buffer cuts $5bn's reach to ~$390bn; a liquidity line from the AAA backer restores it.

slides.source: G20 capital adequacy review (2022); Schlegl, Trebesch and Wright (2019); working paper 4.2, Proposition 1.

slides.title: Holding the cautious buffer, the Trust grows on its own yield if losses follow the banks' record

points.text: grows ~3% a year with no fee; with $95bn private co-investment, $34bn after 10 years.
shrinks 8.5% a year without fees; with $95bn co-investment, levels off near $28bn.

slides.source: Author's calculation; fee 25% of a 10% return; FMO (2019).

slides.title: A feebate between accounts rewards performance at no net cost

stats.label: net cost: credits below the average intensity equal debits above it
highest feasible rate at launch ($5bn in ten accounts)

slides.text: Delay forfeits credits every year, so waiting is never free. While the Trust holds the cautious buffer, high-intensity countries join only at low rates: give entrants a transitional benchmark that converges on a published schedule.
slides.source: Working paper 4.2, Proposition 3; stylized ten-country power sector, 0.3–0.9 tCO₂/MWh.

slides.title: Precedents show each piece works; none does all three jobs

points.text: the G20 review (2022) and SDR hybrid capital (up to SDR 15bn, May 2024) stretch it, inside the banks.
loan, deposit and reserve accounts; $48.9bn pledged by July 2025; owed back to contributors.
$25bn sponsor capital, repaid over 30 years after 10 years' grace, beneath up to $100bn senior debt; about $4 a hectare; pays out, insures nothing.
bonds against binding pledges, with a reserve held back.

slides.source: IMF (2022, 2025); TFFF Concept Note 3.0 (2025); Plant (2024); IFFIm.
